docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
HRV-Longitudinal-Analyzer has been developed as a modular scientific application for organizing, processing and analysing longitudinal heart rate variability (HRV) data.

The public version has been designed to provide a simple and reproducible workflow while preserving participant confidentiality.

docs.title: main_public.py
docs.text:
Main application entry point.

Responsible for controlling the complete workflow, from data import to result generation.

docs.title: config.py
docs.text: Contains the project configuration parameters used during execution.

docs.title: Datos_publicos
docs.text:
Input directory containing the HRV reports exported from Kubios HRV Software.

The software automatically detects all compatible files.

docs.title: Resultados_publicos
docs.text:
Output directory.

All generated datasets and reports are automatically stored here.

docs.title: Processing workflow
docs.text:
The software performs the following steps automatically:

  1. Read the available HRV reports.
  2. Detect all participants.
  3. Organize repeated measurements.
  4. Apply automatic participant anonymization.
  5. Generate standardized outputs.

docs.title: Anonymization
docs.text:
The public version replaces every participant identifier with anonymous labels:

Subject_001
Subject_002
Subject_003
...

No personal identifiers are included in the generated outputs.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
The software has been developed following the principles of:

  • Simplicity
  • Reproducibility
  • Standardization
  • Open Science
  • Data confidentiality

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Place one or more Kubios HRV reports from the same participant inside:

Datos_publicos

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
Run:

python main_public.py

The software automatically:

  • Imports all reports.
  • Detects the participant.
  • Organizes repeated measurements.
  • Replaces the participant identifier with an anonymous label.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The generated files are saved inside:

Resultados_publicos

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Copy HRV reports from several participants into:

Datos_publicos

The reports may correspond to different assessment days or follow-up sessions.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
The software automatically:

  • Detects every participant.
  • Groups repeated measurements.
  • Assigns anonymous identifiers (Subject_001, Subject_002, ...).
  • Processes the complete longitudinal dataset.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
All processed information is exported to:

Resultados_publicos

docs.title: Example 3 — Scientific collaboration
docs.text:
The public version allows researchers to share datasets without exposing participant identities.

Only anonymized information is included in the generated outputs, facilitating reproducible analyses and collaborative research.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Export HRV reports from Kubios HRV Software.
  2. Copy the reports into Datos_publicos.
  3. Run main_public.py.
  4. Review the generated outputs in Resultados_publicos.

docs.title: Which HRV software is supported?
docs.text: The current version processes reports exported from Kubios HRV Software.

docs.title: Does the software modify the original files?
docs.text:
No.

The original HRV reports are never modified.

docs.title: Where should the HRV reports be placed?
docs.text:
Copy all exported reports into:

Datos_publicos

before running the software.

docs.title: Where are the results stored?
docs.text:
All generated outputs are automatically saved in:

Resultados_publicos

docs.title: Is participant anonymization automatic?
docs.text:
Yes.

Every detected participant is automatically assigned an anonymous identifier (Subject_001, Subject_002, ...).

docs.title: Can the software analyse multiple participants?
docs.text:
Yes.

The software automatically detects and processes one or many participants without requiring additional configuration.

docs.title: Can longitudinal measurements be analysed?
docs.text:
Yes.

The software is specifically designed for repeated HRV assessments collected over time.

docs.title: Are the generated outputs suitable for scientific research?
docs.text:
Yes.

The public version has been designed to generate standardized and anonymized outputs that facilitate reproducibility and scientific collaboration.

docs.title: Is any personal information included in the public version?
docs.text:
No.

The repository and the generated outputs are intended for public distribution and do not contain participant-identifiable information.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
HRV-Longitudinal-Analyzer requires:

  • Python 3.11 or later
  • Windows operating system
  • Kubios HRV reports exported in the supported format

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download the project.
  2. Extract the compressed file.
  3. Install the required Python packages:
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.text:

main_public.py

docs.text:
All generated files are automatically stored inside:

The original HRV reports are never modified.

docs.text: Replace the project files with the latest release while preserving your input and output folders if required.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
HRV-Longitudinal-Analyzer has been developed to automate the organization and processing of longitudinal heart rate variability (HRV) datasets exported from Kubios HRV Software.

The public version performs all processing automatically while preserving participant confidentiality.

docs.title: Input data
docs.text:
The software reads all compatible HRV reports located inside:

Datos_publicos

No manual configuration of the files is required.

docs.title: Processing pipeline
docs.text:
During execution the software automatically performs the following operations:

  1. File detection.
  2. Data import.
  3. Participant identification.
  4. Longitudinal organization of repeated measurements.
  5. Automatic participant anonymization.
  6. Data validation.
  7. Output generation.

docs.title: Participant anonymization
docs.text:
Each detected participant is assigned a unique anonymous identifier.

Example:

Subject_001
Subject_002
Subject_003

The original participant names are never included in the generated outputs.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
All generated files are stored inside:

Resultados_publicos

The original HRV reports remain unchanged.

docs.title: Software philosophy
docs.text:
The public version has been designed to provide:

  • Standardized processing.
  • Automatic anonymization.
  • Reproducible analyses.
  • Scientific transparency.
  • Easy distribution for research and teaching.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
HRV-Longitudinal-Analyzer is designed to automate the organization and longitudinal analysis of heart rate variability (HRV) data exported from Kubios HRV Software.

The public version allows researchers, teachers and students to analyse complete datasets while preserving participant confidentiality through automatic anonymization.

docs.title: Before starting
docs.text:
Verify that the following elements are present in the project folder:

  • main_public.py
  • config.py
  • Datos_publicos
  • Resultados_publicos

docs.title: Preparing the data
docs.text:
Copy all Kubios HRV reports into the Datos_publicos folder.

The software automatically detects all available files during execution.

No manual file organization is required.

docs.title: Running the software
docs.text:
Execute:

main_public.py

The program automatically:

  • Reads all available HRV reports.
  • Detects every participant.
  • Organizes repeated measurements.
  • Replaces participant identifiers with anonymous labels.
  • Processes the complete dataset.
  • Generates the corresponding outputs.

docs.title: Generated results
docs.text:
All outputs are automatically saved inside:

Resultados_publicos

Depending on the analysed dataset, the software may generate tables, longitudinal databases and additional scientific outputs.

docs.title: Participant anonymization
docs.text:
The public version never exports personal identifiers.

Every participant is automatically renamed using anonymous labels:

Subject_001
Subject_002
Subject_003
...

This procedure allows datasets to be shared without revealing participant identity.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Export HRV reports from Kubios.
  2. Copy the reports into Datos_publicos.
  3. Run main_public.py.
  4. Retrieve the generated outputs from Resultados_publicos.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Keep the original Kubios reports unchanged.
  • Do not modify automatically generated files.
  • Preserve the project folder structure.
  • Use the generated outputs for research, teaching or collaborative projects.

docs.title: Current version
docs.text:
The current public version provides:

  • Automatic import of Kubios HRV reports.
  • Longitudinal organization of repeated measurements.
  • Automatic participant anonymization.
  • Standardized scientific outputs.
  • Public distribution compatible with Open Science principles.

docs.title: Future developments
docs.text:
The following improvements are planned for future releases:

  • Support for additional HRV data sources.
  • Expanded statistical analyses.
  • Additional longitudinal indicators.
  • Improved automatic reporting.
  • Enhanced graphical outputs.
  • New export formats.
  • Performance optimizations.

docs.title: Project vision
docs.text:
HRV-Longitudinal-Analyzer aims to become an open scientific platform for the standardized processing and longitudinal analysis of heart rate variability data.

The project will continue to prioritize:

  • Scientific reproducibility.
  • Data confidentiality.
  • Ease of use.
  • Open Science.
  • Long-term sustainability.
